sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.21835 of 2013
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioners, seeking the following relief:
"...to issue an appropriate Writ, Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondents for non-payment of balance compensation amount Rs.10,08,000/- along with accrued Interest to the Petitioners in terms of Consent Award dated 23/01/2008 of the 3rd Respondent and also the Award dated 30/06/2011 of the Civil Court in L.A.O.P.
No.773/2009 on the file of the Hon'ble Chairman, Land Appellate Tribunal-Cum-II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District, NTR Nagar, Hyderabad as illegal,
void without jurisdiction and violative of principles of natural justice and consequently direct the Respondents to pay the balance compensation amount Rs.10,08,000/- along with accrued Interest @ 24% per annum from the date of Award dated 23/01/2008 to the Petitioners herein immediately and pass..."
2.

It is stated that the petitioners are the absolute owners and possessors of the land to an extent of Ac.1.32 gts in Sy.No.184 situated at Hameedulla Nagar Village, ShamshabadMandal, Ranga Reddy District.
It is the case of the petitioners that their names have been recorded in the revenue records as absolute owners and possessors of the land to the said extent and they are in enjoyment of the same.

It is the further case of the petitioners that respondent No.3 issued a notification for acquiring lands of the petitioners, along with 2 CVBR,J wp_21835_2013 other lands, to an extent of Ac.59.31 gts, which are forming part of various survey numbers for the purpose of formation of outer ring road.

It is the further case of the petitioners that respondent No.3 passed consent award vide proceedings No.L.A./Unit-I/14/2005, dated 23.01.2008 in terms of G.O.Ms.No.14, dated 18.12.2006 and in respect of the extent of Ac.1.39 gts in Sy.No.184, a general award was passed fixing the market value at the rate of Rs.4,47,019/- and after deducting income tax, the remaining amount is stated to have been deposited in the Civil Court in view of the disputes between the petitioners and other claimants.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that for the extent in dispute i.e., Ac.1.39 gts., the petitioners are entitled for Rs.22,86,000/- whereas the respondents have deposited Rs.12,77,922/-.

Learned counsel further submitted that in terms of the consent award, the respondents have to release the balance amount of Rs.10,08,000/- and the said amount has to be deposited to the credit of L.A.O.P.No.773 of 2009 where the dispute among the inter se claimants is pending under Section 31 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Learned counsel further submitted that even after acquiring the said land in terms of the G.O.Ms.No.14 dated 18.12.2006, the 3 CVBR,J K. Prameela, R.R. Dist. And Anr vs Prl. Secy., Infrastructure And ... on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25854055/
1 wp_21835_2013 respondents have not deposited the balance amount payable to the petitioners in pursuance of the consent award passed by the respondents on 23.01.2008.

sentences.text:
4. The respondents have filed counter affidavit stating as under:
"It is submitted that the subject land an extent of Ac.6.12 gts in Sy.No.184 of Hameedulla Nagar (V) was acquired for formation of ORRP, out of acquired extent as there was a dispute an extent of Ac.1-39 gts between pattadar and possessors and they were not coming forward to compromise and settle the issue the matter was referred to civil court under Section 30 & 31 of the L.A. Act and was numbered as L.A.O.P. No.773 of 2009 on the file of II Additional District Judge, Rangareddy District, the II Additional District Judge, Rangareddy District has passed orders on calculations and pay an amount for Ac.0-07 gts out of the total compensation deposited, to claimant no.1 and to pay remaining amount to claimants 2 and 3 together by way of joint cheque in the name of the claimants 2 and 3, for their Ac.1.32 gts.
According to said award writ petitioners filed consent application for payment of compensation to an extent of Ac.1.32 gts as per G.O.Ms.No.14 dated 18.12.2006.

As per package, the petitioners are entitled for an amount of Rs.22,86,000/- after deducting the already paid amount of Rs.15,64,087/- by Civil Court the writ petitioners are entitled for remaining amount of (Rs.22,86,000 - 15,64,087 =
7,21,913/-) 7,21,913/- only towards as per the package announced by the government vide G.O.Ms.No.14, dated 18-12-2006."
5. In the counter, the respondents have admitted passing of the consent award and fixing the market value at rate of Rs.22,86,000/-.

It is further stated that after deducting the amount already deposited in L.A.O.P.No.773 of 2009 on the file of the II Additional District Judge, Rangareddy District, the balance amount payable by the respondents is an amount of 4 CVBR,J wp_21835_2013 Rs.7,21,913/- in terms of the package announced by the Government vide G.O.Ms.No.14 dated 18.12.2006.
6.

entities.text: II Additional District Judge, Rangareddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
As the respondents have not raised any dispute for payment of the balance amount to the tune of Rs.7,21,930/-, the respondents are directed to release the balance amount to the petitioners along with 12% interest from the date of passing of the consent award duly obtaining the documents,
which are necessary to show that the petitioners alone are the successor- in-interest of the claimants in L.A.O.P.No.773 of 2009 on the file of the II Additional District Judge, Rangareddy District and if the petitioners are entitled for the same in terms of the award in L.A.O.P.No.773 of 2009, dated 30.06.2011, within eight (08) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
7.
With the above observations, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
